newsitem.title: USA: FCC denies SBC bid for long-distance phone service.
newsitem.headline: FCC denies SBC bid for long-distance phone service.

text.p: Federal phone regulators, in their first such ruling under last year's communications law, Thursday rejected SBC Communications Inc.'s bid to enter the $80 billion long-distance phone business.

The Federal Communications Commission said the San Antonio, Texas-based Baby Bell had failed to meet the law's requirement that it open its own local phone monopoly to competitors seeking to offer local phone service.

SBC, in seeking to offer long-distance service in Oklahoma, argued that it had opened its local phone market in the state to competitors, such as long-distance carriers and cable-television operators.
But the FCC said that SBC had "failed to demonstrate that there is a competing provider of telephone exchange service to both residential and business subscribers in Oklahoma."

The agency also said the carrier failed to meet the so-called "Track B" test in which a Baby Bell can offer long-distance phoning from its local-calling region even when it does not face competition in the local phone market.
And the FCC said SBC failed to meet a 14-point check-list of requirements detailing the opening of local phone monopolies under last year's communications law.
